name: Forehead Wrinkle
description: Evaluates the naturalness of dynamic forehead wrinkle formation during facial expressions, detecting static or incorrectly deforming wrinkle patterns indicative of face reenactment manipulation.
mechanism:
This method specifically analyzes forehead wrinkle dynamics for deepfake detection:

1. **Forehead Wrinkle Detection**: Horizontal forehead wrinkles are detected using oriented ridge detection filters. Each wrinkle is characterized: position (forehead height), depth (shadow contrast), length (ear-to-ear extent), and curvature (following frontal bone contour).

2. **Frontalis-Wrinkle Biomechanics**: Forehead wrinkles are produced by frontalis muscle contraction. The method verifies biomechanical correctness: (a) wrinkles should be roughly horizontal following frontalis fiber direction, (b) wrinkle spacing reflects the muscle's compartmentalized structure, (c) wrinkle depth should correlate with brow elevation magnitude. Deepfakes may produce wrinkles with incorrect orientation or depth.

3. **Dynamic Wrinkle Behavior**: As the brow raises, wrinkles deepen and become more visible; as the brow relaxes, they flatten. The method tracks the temporal correlation between brow position (AU1/AU2) and wrinkle visibility. Low correlation indicates the face generator produces wrinkles independently of expression.

4. **Wrinkle Pattern Individual Consistency**: Each person has a characteristic forehead wrinkle pattern determined by muscle anatomy and skin elasticity. The method checks whether the wrinkle pattern remains consistent across frames. Deepfakes may produce varying wrinkle patterns frame-to-frame, especially when combining different source identities.

5. **Wrinkle Rendering Assessment**: The 3D appearance of wrinkles (shadow on the upper edge, highlight on the lower edge in downward illumination) should be consistent with scene lighting. The method evaluates wrinkle rendering quality and lighting consistency. AI-generated wrinkles may show physically incorrect shadow patterns.
parameters:
Analysis type: pixel
Media: video
Input: Video frames extracted at key intervals
Output: Confidence score (0-100)
Frame sampling: Adaptive (1-5 fps depending on method)
Temporal window: Sliding window across frame sequence
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-88% standalone accuracy. Most effective when combined with other video forensic methods. Performance depends on video quality, resolution, and compression level.
source: Video forensics and deepfake detection research. Based on computer vision and temporal signal analysis methods.
useCase: Detection of deepfake and AI-generated video through forehead wrinkle analysis. This method examines temporal and spatial features that are difficult for AI systems to perfectly replicate, providing evidence for video authenticity assessment.
strengths:
• Captures temporal artifacts that single-frame analysis misses
• Works with standard video formats
• Effective against common deepfake techniques
• Can be combined with other video forensic methods
• Based on established computer vision research
limitations:
• Performance affected by video compression and resolution
• Some methods require sufficient frame count for temporal analysis
• Effectiveness varies with deepfake generation technique
• Best used as part of a comprehensive multi-method pipeline
• May produce false positives on heavily edited authentic video
